entries.title: Jet Set Radio
entries.lesson: SEGA's original street-action identity combines inline skating, a stylized city and graffiti.
entries.application: Treat the existing paint, skating, dance and music systems as one street identity. Make a tag's location memorable through the line needed to reach it.
entries.prototype: Build three tag spots with distinct approaches: street rail, wall-kick corner and roof transfer. Ask players to describe the location after one visit.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Jet Set Radio Future
entries.lesson: SEGA's original manual documents trick/combo moves, free skating, a garage, graffiti editing and versus missions.
entries.application: Use the garage/hangout as a physical place to practice existing tricks, choose art and meet crews, with immediate return to movement.
entries.prototype: Place a small practice loop beside a Boombox and paint wall. Measure how many menu exits and travel steps a new player needs to try a move.
entries.evidence: SEGA manual, hosted mirror; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Bomb Rush Cyberfunk
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: Team Reptile documents linked tricks, grinding, sliding, wallrunning, graffiti spots and REP-based crew challenges.
entries.application: Refine the already-approved boostpack and gang progression around useful lines between objectives. Reward reaching new surfaces and connecting movement families.
entries.prototype: Compare a direct flat route with a rail–wall–roof route to the same tag. Check time, Flow, boost use and players' preferred route.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: HYPERFUNK
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer advertises combo-dependent boost speed, dynamic crew territory, four graffiti classes and online hangouts.
entries.application: Use this as a current research target for the already-approved pack/crew systems. Prototype readable escalation and deliberate tag-size tradeoffs inside valid event surfaces.
entries.prototype: Compare three boost-response curves at the same maximum safe speed; compare quick small tags versus slower high-value murals without rewarding idle spam.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Hover
entries.lesson: The publisher describes a vertical open city, single/multiplayer challenges, first/third-person views and an in-game challenge editor.
entries.application: Give a player-built district multiple activities using the same route graph: race, chase, trick line and courier objective. Keep route authoring compact.
entries.prototype: Author one bounded loop once, then replay it as time trial and chase. Record which route metadata can be shared and which rules must differ.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Rooftops & Alleys
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer lists free roaming, hidden spots, time trials, trick challenges, Tag, Capture the Flag and trick battles.
entries.application: Improve discovery and session recovery for already-approved challenge families. A good roof should support practice, competition and hanging out without separate world copies.
entries.prototype: Build a roof plaza with a reset marker, two race branches and a Tag loop. Time how quickly friends can retry or switch activities.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Rollerdrome
entries.lesson: Roll7 explains that varied trick chains replenish ammunition; wallrides, grinds and grabs keep offense and movement interacting.
entries.application: Directly support the approved trick-ammo/TaCZ loop. Tune the opportunity to resupply around safe-but-not-free traversal windows and weapon-specific accounting.
entries.prototype: In one arena compare direct-magazine and reserve replenishment. Measure dry-fire time, reload interruptions, trick variety and duplicate reward attempts.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Sunset Overdrive
entries.lesson: The official store describes combat across a city using grinding, vaulting and wallrunning.
entries.application: Make combat routes circulate around cover and escape options. Preserve weapon control while lower-body movement remains expressive.
entries.prototype: Create a three-height combat loop with two escape paths per pressure point. Check aiming/reload ownership during every movement transition.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2
entries.lesson: Activision lists original game modes, Create-A-Park, Create-A-Skater, online multiplayer and leaderboards.
entries.application: Teach the existing trick grammar through small repeatable spots with several goals, then let builders remix those spots in their own worlds.
entries.prototype: One plaza supports a clean landing goal, a variety goal and a connected-line goal. Check that one exploit loop cannot satisfy all three.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Session: Skate Sim
entries.lesson: The official site emphasizes skating culture and a video editor for filming player-created lines.
entries.application: Make self-directed practice feel worthwhile alongside progression: clean retries, chosen camera angles and clips of personally satisfying lines.
entries.prototype: Test a local practice marker and capture workflow on one stair–rail spot. Measure retry time and camera obstruction without modifying score authority.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: OlliOlli World
entries.lesson: The official product page highlights accessible skating, deeper combo mastery, alternate paths and expressive customization.
entries.application: Separate ordinary completion from optional mastery on the same circuit. Existing ride variety should create alternate solutions rather than exclude beginners.
entries.prototype: Give one course finish, variety and expert-transfer medals. Verify a beginner can finish without the expert route while experts still have a reason to replay.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Skate Story
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer frames skating through a surreal underworld as a journey from fragile beginner to skilled skater.
entries.application: Use temporary boss arenas or dreamlike event spaces for bold atmosphere while maintaining clear surfaces and consistent ride control.
entries.prototype: Create one short reflective/void-themed line. Compare readability with effects low/high and check that the visual spectacle never conceals the landing.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Helskate
entries.lesson: Its store describes tricks and combos powering attacks in a skateboarding action roguelite.
entries.application: Study optional event modifiers for the approved survival modes: a different tactical rhythm per run without permanently distorting free-roam handling.
entries.prototype: Compare two disclosed event loadouts, one rewarding transfers and one varied air tricks; check whether either collapses into repeatable trivial farming.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Driftwood
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer emphasizes downhill longboarding, drift control, board/wheel combinations and relaxed or competitive sessions.
entries.application: Refine board carving and powerslide identity. The live wiki already treats longboard/surfskate as variants before adding another base ride ID.
entries.prototype: Use the same winding slope with two board setups. Record entry speed, turn radius, drift angle, exit speed and recovery after oversteer.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: BMX Streets
entries.lesson: The developer emphasizes control on ground, in the air and on handrails, plus meaningful bike customization.
entries.application: Give the existing BMX a distinctive transfer, peg and landing vocabulary. Tie parts to understandable handling tradeoffs, not only bigger speed numbers.
entries.prototype: Compare a ledge line and a gap line with two BMX setups. Assess silhouette, landing feedback, steering commitment and item-use compatibility.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: ScooterFlow
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The current store lists physical scooter tricks, customization, multiplayer sessions, real parks and replay editing.
entries.application: Deepen the existing scooter with readable tailwhip/barspin combinations and compact transfers. Preserve keyboard play despite this reference requiring a controller.
entries.prototype: Film the same short quarter-to-ledge line in first and third person. Can testers identify the scooter move and landing grade without reading HUD labels?
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Neon White
entries.lesson: The official description centers on speedrunning and sacrificing weapon cards for parkour moves.
entries.application: Improve route iteration: short attempts, transparent objective completion and a visible next improvement. Keep JetSetCraft's accepted TaCZ economy distinct.
entries.prototype: Build a 30–60-second timed line with one optional shortcut and three checkpoints. Compare restart friction and clarity of a missed checkpoint.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Mirror's Edge Catalyst
entries.lesson: EA describes configurable Runner's Vision: Off, Classic and Full View, using highlighted route objects and a trail.
entries.application: Add optional course guidance levels using shapes, signs and concise prompts as well as color. Free exploration should remain possible with guidance disabled.
entries.prototype: Run the same course with guidance off, minimal and full. Measure wrong turns and whether guidance teaches landmarks that remain useful afterward.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Cyber Hook
entries.lesson: The developer advertises grappling, wall traversal, physics-based route choice, leaderboards and a level editor.
entries.application: Study release direction and momentum transfer when interoperating with optional grapples or flight. No new mandatory grapple dependency is implied.
entries.prototype: Test compatible grapple release into a JetSetCraft grind and grind exit into flight. Record lost velocity and unintended automatic reattachment.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Pseudoregalia
entries.lesson: The developer describes open-ended 3D Metroidvania routes and a movement vocabulary including air kicks.
entries.application: Use the existing wall-kick/vault grammar and approved progression to reveal new ways through familiar places. Distinguish skill shortcuts from hard equipment gates.
entries.prototype: Build a courtyard with a basic route and a demanding wall sequence. Confirm the advanced path uses legal actions and remains comprehensible without invisible barriers.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Solar Ash
entries.lesson: The official store describes rail grinding, grappling, cloud surfing and enormous bosses in a high-speed world.
entries.application: Shape boss arenas as movement puzzles with clear approach, attack and recovery routes. Scale can come from architecture and presentation before moving whole terrain.
entries.prototype: Prototype a static giant-shaped arena with three connected target lanes. Check that the camera keeps the next valid surface visible at intended speed.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Haste
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer highlights high speed, airborne travel, mastering landings and procedural worlds, solo or with friends.
entries.application: Refine existing landing grades and approved runner circuits around prediction and recovery. Make good landings visibly preserve a line.
entries.prototype: Test an authored sequence of three descending landings at several entry speeds. Track landing-grade agreement, maintained speed and recovery-line use.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Refunct
entries.lesson: The creator describes a short, peaceful first-person platformer about restoring a vibrant world.
entries.application: Use a pressure-free micro-course to teach one existing action at a time before combining them. Let completion visibly change the practice space.
entries.prototype: Create a five-station skate tutorial using safe returns and optional repeated practice. Count first-session failures and requests for a controls menu.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom
entries.lesson: Its developer describes a collectathon whose movement combinations reach unusual places without a jump button.
entries.application: Use the approved crate/coin platforming modes to reward creative combinations of existing actions. Collectibles should advertise reachable lines, not arbitrary detours.
entries.prototype: Place optional event coins along two legal approach arcs to one rooftop. Check that a clever route earns recognition and required quotas remain achievable.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: SLUDGE LIFE
entries.lesson: The developer presents a compact, polluted open world centered on exploration, graffiti and eccentric inhabitants.
entries.application: Make graffiti placement tell a local story: hidden wall, visible rooftop statement, crew hangout marker. Reuse the current bounded painting system.
entries.prototype: Design six tag spots in one small district, each with a distinct landmark or social context. Ask which spots players remember and revisit.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Umurangi Generation
entries.lesson: PLAYISM describes photography bounties, flexible composition, exploration bonuses and environmental observation.
entries.application: Give crews observational challenges alongside speed: document a mural, gather friends at a landmark or find a distinctive viewpoint.
entries.prototype: Use a screenshot-based manual playtest first. Validate objective clarity before considering any automated image or composition scoring.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Splatoon 3
entries.lesson: Nintendo explains Turf War as competition to cover ground with ink; its official tips emphasize movement.
entries.application: Support the already-approved Turf War with immediately readable ownership and meaningful route access. JetSetCraft's bounded valid surfaces remain the scoring basis.
entries.prototype: Compare two equal-area arenas with different travel costs to targets. Measure first-arrival advantage and readable capture-state changes, including colorblind presentation.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Sable
entries.lesson: Raw Fury describes exploration, climbing, a customizable hoverbike, helping clans and identity through masks/outfits.
entries.application: Make the approved workshop and gang reputation feel personal through recognizable part silhouettes and meaningful unlock stories, while keeping cosmetic freedom.
entries.prototype: Give two otherwise equivalent rides different crew parts and one memorable unlock challenge each. Test recognition and whether players understand the reward's meaning.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Lorn's Lure
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer describes vast structures and climbing almost any vertical wall with pickaxes, mixing fast and slow traversal.
entries.application: Study industrial route density and visible destinations in caves or megastructures. Use JetSetCraft's existing contact rules rather than adding universal climbing by default.
entries.prototype: Build a three-storey shaft with a clearly visible exit and two routes. Check lost-player time, wall readability and non-lethal recovery options.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: MOTORSLICE
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The developer lists parkour through brutalist structures, massive machine bosses and atmospheric DnB/jungle music.
entries.application: Use machine-scale landmarks, long sightlines and quieter spaces between intense event sections. Apply this to approved boss arenas and industrial biome circuits.
entries.prototype: Build a crane silhouette around a movement course without functional machinery. Test recognition, route visibility and contrast between approach and peak intensity.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: BETON BRUTAL
entries.lesson: The creator explicitly cites Minecraft parkour, an overgrown concrete tower, increasing difficulty and discoverable shortcuts.
entries.application: Study block-readable obstacle composition and vertical landmarks. Keep a forgiving main mode and reserve long progress loss for clearly disclosed expert variants.
entries.prototype: Build a vertical course with visible landing shelves and an optional shortcut. Compare checkpointed practice with an opt-in endurance run using identical geometry.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: White Knuckle
entries.lesson: Its current store describes a first-person roguelite speed-climbing game with precision movement and resource management.
entries.application: Study escalating pursuit and pressured route choice for the already-approved survival mode. Use event pace and telegraphs before inflating enemy counts.
entries.prototype: Prototype one pursuing hazard and two escape routes. Measure reaction time, recoverability and whether failure is attributable to a visible choice.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: A Short Hike
entries.lesson: The creator describes open routes, helpful characters, hidden treasures and music that changes as players explore.
entries.application: Use a compact district with several inviting destinations rather than a sparse giant map. Social and creative progress should share terrain with high-skill skating.
entries.prototype: Build three visible destinations reachable in different ways from a hangout. Observe which path new players choose without objective markers.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Lil Gator Game
entries.lesson: The publisher describes a movement-focused open-world adventure built around helping friends and playful cardboard enemies.
entries.application: Make low-pressure crew interactions useful for onboarding and junior-friendly activities. Reuse normal mobs' identities and the approved reversible challenge flow.
entries.prototype: Run one friendly challenge with a passive mob beside a safe practice route. Check whether the invitation and return to normal behavior are understandable.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Hot Lava
entries.lesson: Klei lists run/jump/climb/swing/surf traversal, drop-in multiplayer, shortcuts and a construction kit.
entries.application: Use one instantly understandable event rule to remix ordinary terrain. For a no-floor-contact variant, use event scoring volumes rather than filling real builds with lava.
entries.prototype: Test a short loop as ordinary race and floor-contact challenge. Verify bystanders/world blocks remain unaffected and failures return the participant safely.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Descenders
entries.lesson: The developer lists procedural downhill routes, freestyle bike controls, run modifiers and teams focused on different riding styles.
entries.application: Refine the approved mountain-bike/mountainboard courses with visibly different technical, speed and trick routes. Offer intentional event variation rather than random clutter.
entries.prototype: Generate the same seed in three route profiles. Compare jump spacing, line curvature, expert choices and successful completion at legal movement speeds.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Lonely Mountains: Downhill
entries.lesson: The official store contrasts scenic routes with hidden shortcuts, responsive riding and distinct bike handling.
entries.application: Make route scouting and quiet free riding valuable alongside competition. An expert shortcut should be visible, risky and locally recoverable.
entries.prototype: Create a forest descent with a safe trail and a shorter rock line. Measure completion consistency and test whether players can inspect the shortcut before committing.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Riders Republic
entries.lesson: Ubisoft presents a shared multisport world; its official launch materials describe career tracks, group events and a social hub.
entries.application: Support the already-approved mixed-ride/wingsuit system with readable transitions and visible gathering points. Do not infer support for huge player counts in Forge.
entries.prototype: Prototype one two-discipline event with declared equipment rules and a safe transition zone. Check controller ownership, combo continuity and spectators' understanding.
entries.evidence: Developer, publisher or official store; research comparison, not installed-game measurements.

entries.title: Denshattack!
entries.image_credit: Official publisher/developer store artwork
entries.lesson: The current official store describes train flips, tricks, grinding, customization, rival gangs and varied Japanese environments.
entries.application: Research input-to-response and visual readability for the existing Trick Trains/Create goal and issue #37. The catalogue does not reopen approval or claim an adapter is finished.
entries.prototype: Record reference maneuvers from the owner-authorized installed build, then compare a bounded JetSetCraft train prototype: response, rotation, landing and rider handoff.

entries.title: Java 17 — CompletableFuture
entries.lesson: CompletableFuture composes asynchronous work and explicit executors. Its documentation distinguishes execution policies and notes that cancellation is a completion mechanism rather than a guarantee that underlying work is interrupted.
entries.application: Load metadata and decode suitable assets off the render thread, then publish immutable results only if their world, pack and screen generation are still current. Keep texture creation and Minecraft state mutation on the appropriate owning thread.
entries.prototype: Delay an old load, switch asset packs or worlds, and let the old work finish last. The result must be discarded without replacing newer state; corrupt or missing content should retain stable IDs and display a useful fallback.

entries.lesson: The paper replaces components of a motion-matching pipeline with learned models, investigating how a responsive animation controller can use a motion database more compactly.

entries.title: Robust Motion In-betweening
entries.artist: Félix G. Harvey, Mike Yurick, Derek Nowrouzezahrai and Christopher Pal
entries.lesson: The authors study learned motion transitions constrained by starting and target motion, introducing time-to-arrival conditioning and the LaFAN1 benchmark for evaluating in-betweening.

entries.prototype: Author bridges from coast to trick preparation, trick to landing and dance to neutral. Compare with a simple blend, and reject transitions that slide planted feet, delay a cancel or take ownership of combat arms.

entries.title: Phase-Functioned Neural Networks for Character Control
entries.artist: Daniel Holden, Taku Komura and Jun Saito
entries.lesson: The paper uses phase-dependent neural control to relate character animation to user commands and terrain geometry. The author project demonstrates the role of locomotion phase in terrain-aware character motion.
entries.application: Treat push phase, foot-contact phase and slope as useful animation metadata even if no neural runtime is adopted. Use them to improve pose alignment while the existing movement system continues to determine speed, stopping and fluid behavior.

entries.lesson: The research models character interaction with scene geometry, including actions involving chairs, boxes and doors. It provides a concrete study of animation conditioned on an intended interaction and its surroundings.
